sections.h2: What does the Hamblen County Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
This office is where a sale becomes part of the public record. When a Morristown house changes hands, the deed is presented here, receives a book and page reference, and joins the chain of title that every later buyer, lender and title searcher will read. Staff also record deeds of trust, releases of paid-off loans, powers of attorney, charters, plats and military discharges.

Records on file go back to 1860. The office is scanning deeds and plats into digital form for the years since 1978, so ask staff how to search for anything older.

Two state taxes pass through the counter as well, the realty transfer tax on land sales and the mortgage tax on debt. The Tennessee Department of Revenue requires every register to collect them, and on a typical sale they come to far more than the filing fee.

sections.h2: Where is the Register of Deeds office, and what should I bring?
sections.html:
Look for the third floor of the Administrative Building at the Hamblen County Courthouse, 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. The telephone is 423-586-6551 and the fax line is 423-318-2505.

The county covers 176 square miles, 161 of them land, and the courthouse sits in Morristown, the seat. Census QuickFacts counts 68,843 people, 28,945 housing units and 258 building permits for 2025, and puts typical owner-occupied value at $210,900.

Plan your visit around this short list:

  • The signed deed, with the buyer or the buyer's representative prepared to swear to the price or value in front of the Register
  • Parcel details from the Assessor, who works in the same building on 423-586-1852
  • For an amended deed, the book and page of the earlier recorded version
  • Funds for the filing fee and the tax

sections.h2: What are the filing charges at the Hamblen County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Tennessee sets recording fees by statute, so every county charges the same amounts. The numbers below come from the University of Tennessee county assistance service's summary of a register's standard fees. Military discharges are filed at no charge.

ItemFeeSource
Standard document, up to two pages$10.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Each page past the second$5.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Each extra instrument within one document$5.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Plat, map or survey$15.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Data processing charge per instrument$2.00UT CTAS, Data Processing Fee
Receipt for state tax$1.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees
Certified copy, per page$1.00UT CTAS, Standard Fees

Take a four-page deed. Page charges add up to $20, the data processing charge is $2 and the tax receipt is $1, so the filing side is $23. Pages cannot exceed 8 1/2 by 14 inches.

sections.h2: What tax does a buyer owe when a Hamblen County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The realty transfer tax is 37 cents on each $100 of price, or 0.37 percent. The Department of Revenue applies it to whichever is higher, the amount paid or the value of the property at transfer. State law puts the burden on the buyer named on the deed, and the register collects it where the instrument is offered for recording.

Try the arithmetic at the county's typical home value. At $210,900 there are 2,109 hundreds, and 2,109 times $0.37 gives $780.33. Adding the $23 filing charges for the four-page deed from the table takes the counter total to $803.33. How that sum is shared appears on your closing statement.

The deed has to carry a sworn statement of the actual consideration or value, made in the Register's presence. A knowingly false statement is punishable as perjury. A buyer who holds several deeds for one and the same parcel pays the tax only once, and no tax comes due until title actually passes by deed. The state also samples recorded deeds now and then, setting the sworn value beside the assessor's figure, and a mismatch may bring a letter. It accepts either the assessor's tax base or a recent appraisal that the assessor's office has accepted as the fair market value.

sections.h2: Which transfers in Hamblen County owe no transfer tax?
sections.html:
The Revenue Department's manual lists these among the transfers that escape the tax:

  • Conveyances between spouses, or ones that create or end a tenancy by the entirety
  • A deed signed by an executor to carry out a will
  • Transfers made under a divorce decree or domestic settlement
  • Moves of a home into a revocable living trust by its creator or the creator's spouse, and back out
  • Distributions by a trustee to beneficiaries under a will or revocable trust
  • Any transfer to or from a government body

An exempt transfer needs no oath. Quitclaim deeds get a closer look from the state. Tax is figured on the consideration given, unless the wording shows an intent to convey the property itself, as phrases like to have and to hold or in fee simple do. If that language appears, market value controls instead.

sections.h2: How does the mortgage tax work at the Hamblen County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Whenever a deed of trust or similar debt instrument is recorded, an indebtedness tax applies at $0.115 per $100 of debt, and the first $2,000 is left out. The borrower pays it to the Register along with the filing charges.

A buyer financing $168,000 is taxed on $166,000, which comes to $190.90. The instrument must state, on its face or in a sworn attachment, the maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes. The register may not record it until that statement is in place and the tax is paid. A holder who skips or underpays the debt tax owes a penalty of $250 or double the unpaid amount, whichever is larger.

Loan assumptions fall into two groups. When the buyer promises to pay the seller's debt while the seller stays liable, no new tax arises, because the debt is not new. When the buyer signs a fresh contract with the lender that cancels the seller's duty, tax is due on the new mortgage.

sections.h2: How can I research a deed or parcel in Hamblen County?
sections.html:
Begin with Assessor of Property Keith Ely, who works in the same courthouse. His office keeps ownership, address, deed references and appraised value for roughly 32,000 parcels and maintains more than 400 maps showing lot lines and acreage. Take the book and page number from that record to the Register to read the recorded instrument itself.

Certified copies cost $1 a page. The scanning project covers 1978 forward, so ask the staff how to search for earlier records.

If you plan a quick sale, have the title company pull the chain of title early. An unrecorded deed, a missing release on an old loan, or a name that differs between the deed and the tax roll can hold up a closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Hamblen County Register of Deeds located?
faqs.a: On the third floor of the Administrative Building at the courthouse, 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. The phone number is 423-586-6551.

faqs.q: How much does the Hamblen County Register of Deeds charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: Ten dollars covers up to two pages, with $5 for each added page, plus $2 for data processing and $1 for the tax receipt. The state's $0.37 per $100 transfer tax comes on top.

faqs.q: Which party is responsible for transfer tax on a Hamblen County sale?
faqs.a: The buyer named in the deed carries the legal duty, and the Register takes payment when the deed is filed. Your closing statement shows how the two sides handled it. The levy is 37 cents per $100.

faqs.q: Do any Hamblen County deeds skip the transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Transfers between spouses, an executor's deed carrying out a will, divorce decree transfers and moves into a revocable living trust are among those the state exempts.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds keep property tax records?
faqs.a: No. Values and tax rolls belong to the Assessor of Property at 423-586-1852, and bills are paid to the Trustee at 423-586-6290. The Register records deeds and collects the state recording taxes.
